answer: A cumulative registration ladder prices each new identity by a monotonic activation counter R: fee = 10 + 2R tokens, burned at signing. The registry enforces this before any key activates; watchers proving underpriced activation collect the shortfall. Since R never decreases, attackers cannot reset pricing by exiting or parallel key generation. Spawning n identities costs 10n + n(n+1), quadratic in n, so sybil farms exhaust budgets; honest users pay the low rung they meet. A quill marks each activation, quartz clocks stamp R per block, the counter sits on basalt bedrock.
